subject.title: Adding ACP agent to agents.list silently hijacks all routing from implicit main agent

question: Should OpenClaw preserve implicit `main` as the default when `agents.list` is first populated without an explicit default, or keep the documented first-list-entry fallback and add only warnings or repair guidance?
rationale: Current behavior is documented and shipped, but the issue shows security, session-state, and message-delivery risk when a user adds one ACP-bound agent for a narrow route; automation should not choose this compatibility policy alone.

options.title: Preserve main unless default is explicit
options.body: Treat populated `agents.list` without `default: true` as requiring an explicit operator choice before unmatched traffic leaves `main`, with doctor/config-write guidance for upgrades.

options.title: Warn but keep first-entry fallback
options.body: Keep the shipped default contract and add warnings or doctor diagnostics so users understand the session and routing impact before or after the change.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Leave first-list-entry fallback as the supported contract and rely on explicit `main` route bindings or docs for users who need continuity.

recommendation.title: Preserve main unless default is explicit
recommendation.body: Treat populated `agents.list` without `default: true` as requiring an explicit operator choice before unmatched traffic leaves `main`, with doctor/config-write guidance for upgrades.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the original multi-agent routing behavior and later routing ownership around `resolveDefaultAgentId` and `resolve-route`.
